title: Scrape a failed print's cured raft off a Form 4 tank film, lift it out on the blade and bin it without gouging the film
instruction: The print failed and its cured raft is stuck to the film in the resin tank. Without touching anything in the tank with your grippers, clear the raft into the waste tray, leave the film undamaged, and put the tool you used back in its rest.
context: Robot labs print grippers, fingers and brackets on resin printers such as the Formlabs Form 4. A failed print leaves cured resin stuck to the tank film, and the printer makes no more parts until it is off; Formlabs lists it first among tank faults. Its steps: "Scrape laterally using the flat side of the tool to get its edge under the cured resin", "Avoid using the corners", "Do not use a metal tool". A gouged tank "requires immediate disposal".
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the bench. (1) Printer, fixed: Formlabs Form 4 (39.8 W x 36.7 D x 55.4 H cm, 18.3 kg), front face at x 21.0, centred at y 6.0, front toward the robot; cover swung open; build platform, mixer and resin cartridge taken off. (2) Resin tank, fixed: Formlabs Form 4 Resin Tank (RT-F4-01), seated and latched, drained; its clear film 20.5 cm above the bench; well 15.0 x 25.0 cm (x 26.5 to 41.5, y -6.5 to 18.5), walls 3.2 cm above the film (heights and well size are estimates). (3) Cured raft, stuck to the film: a Formlabs Grey V5 resin coupon standing in for a failed print's raft, 50 x 60 x 8 mm, its film-side edge chamfered 45 degrees for 3 mm all round, 27 g (STL in fixture/); long side left-right, 12 mm in front of the well's back wall, centred at x 37.8, y 12.0. (4) The Form 4 Finish Kit's two scrapers, loose, each leaning blade-down at 45 degrees in a printed PLA rest (drawing and STL in fixture/), blade pointing at the printer, edge 1 cm above the bench and 3 cm in front of the printer: white plastic tank scraper (130 mm long, blade 55 mm wide, 25 g; estimates) at y 12.0; stainless metal scraper (165 mm long, blade 40 mm wide, 68 g; estimates) at y 23.5. (5) Waste tray, fixed (taped): Thermo Scientific Nalgene 6902-1000 polypropylene tray, 26.0 x 15.9 x 6.4 cm, long side along x, centred at x 33.5, y 40.0. Both arms start at their rest pose. The layout is the same every trial; run with object_jitter=0.
scoring: Score 0, for the whole trial, if at any moment: a gripper touches the tank film, or touches the raft while it is in the tank (video; in simulation any sampled gripper point within 2 mm); the metal scraper's blade goes below the tank's rim inside the tank (video); the plastic scraper's edge touches the film tilted 10 degrees or more across its width, so one corner bears (front video stepped frame by frame; in simulation one corner within 1.5 mm of the film and the other 9.6 mm or more higher); or any point of its edge is on the film with the blade steeper than 50 degrees (side video). In real trials also 0 for any new gouge, dent, crease or puncture in the film (10x loupe with a phone light under the film, against the before photo). Otherwise, at the end: 1.0: the raft lies inside the waste tray's walls (photo from above), the plastic scraper is back in its rest (edge within 15 mm of its marked spot, turned no more than 10 degrees: photo with a steel rule), both grippers 30 mm or more from it, everything still for 1 s (video). 0.75: the raft in the tray and still for 1 s, not being carried on a scraper still in hand; the scraper not back. 0.5: the same, but the raft out of the tank and not in the tray (on the printer, the bench); out of the tank means its middle outside the well seen from above, or more than 1 cm above its rim. 0.25: the raft has come free of the film at some moment: moved 3 mm or turned 3 degrees from where it was stuck (overhead video against the before photo). 0: still stuck.
run_limit: 1,600 steps (80 s at 20 Hz); one trial per simulator launch
reset_notes: 1. Take the tank out, drain it into its resin cartridge, wipe the film with IPA on a lint-free cloth and let it dry (Formlabs' own film-cleaning steps). 2. Photograph the film over a phone light through a 10x loupe (the before photo). 3. Push the placing template (fixture/) into the well's back-left corner, put 0.3 mL of fresh Grey V5 resin in its window, lay a new coupon on it chamfer down, lift the template off, wipe away any resin squeezed out round the coupon. 4. Cure the bond from below through the film: the tank on two blocks, an ULTRAFIRE 501UV-395 PRO UV torch (395-405 nm) 30 mm under the coupon for 20 s. Check with a spring scale: a 5 N push on the coupon's side does not move it. 5. Re-seat and latch the tank; cover open; platform, mixer and cartridge out. 6. Lean both scrapers in their rests, edges against the lips; empty the tray. 7. Simulation: every launch is one trial (the bond is not re-made inside a run).
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim (PhysX). The raft is held to the film by one breakable joint standing in for adhesion (estimates: lets go at 60 N of shear or 0.04 N m of bending, a few N on a blade under one edge); peel progress and wet resin are not modelled. The film is rigid: film damage is judged in simulation by the corner and angle rules, in real trials by the loupe. The tank is drained (no liquid). Deck height, well size and scraper sizes are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (ran all 1,600 steps without refusing; it moved toward the scrapers but picked neither up, and the raft stayed stuck); demo: 1.0 (869 steps). Both on task.py 65f3a29c.
